findings.title: The transaction schema does not bind each CAS hash pair to its canonical record
findings.reproduction: At exact packet commit 1435af96191fde33556bbb6dc9c3bdaa2549fca3, inspect planning/governance-control-recovery/governance-control-recovery-transaction.v2.schema.json. `$defs.contentBinding.properties.path` references only the generic safe-path definition, and predecessor/successor backlog and state all reference the same unconstrained contentBinding definition. The separate paths object is canonical, but the schema establishes no equality between paths.backlog/paths.state and the paths named beside each rawSha256/canonicalSha256 pair. Construct an otherwise schema-valid transaction, set predecessor.state.path to planning/backlog.yaml and successor.backlog.path to planning/governance-control-recovery/GCR-0002.B00.state.json, and validate it with Draft202012Validator against the transaction schema: the baseline reports zero errors and the swapped content-binding document also reports zero errors. The runtime-v2 transaction variant is looser still, declaring predecessor, successor, activeHold, triggerWitness, paths, durability, recovery, and finalization only as generic objects. A schema-valid manifest can therefore associate the state CAS hashes with backlog bytes or the backlog CAS hashes with state bytes while retaining a canonical-looking paths object. If an implementation follows those manifest bindings during validation, rollback, or recovery, it can authenticate or restore the wrong canonical record, contrary to the R01 requirement for exact path-bound raw/canonical CAS, acceptance criterion 5, and the claimed split-state safety boundary.
findings.requiredRemediation: In a strict-descendant inert packet, make the transaction schema bind each predecessor and successor backlog content record to const planning/backlog.yaml and each state content record to const planning/governance-control-recovery/GCR-0002.B00.state.json, either with distinct backlog/state binding definitions or by removing redundant dynamic path fields and requiring the controller to use only the canonical const paths. Make the runtime-v2 transaction variant enforce the same exact nested transaction shape rather than generic objects, and require gcr2ctl to validate the strict transaction schema before trusting any hash or path. Add focused schema and controller denials for swapped, duplicated, cross-record, omitted, substituted, extra, and redirected content-binding paths, proving byte-stable canonical records. Preserve the R01 and R02 ledgers append-only; a fresh R03 review must explicitly close both GCR-0002-R01-F01 and GCR-0002-R02-F01 before approval is available.

verified: The R02 packet commit is exactly 1435af96191fde33556bbb6dc9c3bdaa2549fca3 on codex/w1-windows-local-runtime and is a strict descendant of the R01 ledger-introduction commit d82a640c8779e6a243edc603fd6a5e686c45622b. The R01 commit is the direct child of exact R01 candidate a1c76d12c5752ad12d63e192adf6cd46b5553772 and adds only planning/governance-control-recovery/GCR-0002.review-R01.json.

The immutable R01 ledger remains byte-identical to its d82a640 Git blob with SHA-256 85c28dcea84b56fad6080b95394788e42583079dce24b6f2e5b9fe50d151b621. The R02 packet names that exact path, hash, and commit in packetReviewHistory; no R01 byte or history was rewritten.

The R01-ledger-to-R02-candidate delta is exactly six paths: modified proposal, packet, request-v2 schema, runtime-v2 schema, and static review page plus added governance-control-recovery-transaction.v2.schema.json. No controller, backlog, canonical state, approval, GRR, supplement, amendment, task, gate, product, generated view, or witness byte changed.

The revised packet SHA-256 is exactly 06efe3268d2087b28f5decd3c56d94c4ee5ecb43584baba004175ce5de342f77. It validates with zero Draft 2020-12 errors; the request, runtime, and transaction schemas pass metaschema validation; and every declared file hash matches current bytes.

The broad GCR-0002-R01-F01 remediation is now explicit and consistent across packet, proposal, request schema, runtime schema, transaction schema, and review page: canonical GCR-0002 manifest/lock/backlog-next/state-next paths; exclusive locking; raw and canonical hashes; predecessor 8 and successor 9; exact active hold and trigger; durable successor and prepared-manifest ordering; Windows replace-existing/write-through and file/directory flush duties; explicit idempotent recover and automatic mutation preflight; fail-closed partial, split, missing-marker, stale, substituted, and dirty states; cleanup only after a validated pair; real child-process abrupt-boundary tests; and direct-child exact two-path finalization.

The revised packet preserves the exact authority/evidence chain through approved-state and adoption-evidence commit bindings, predecessor backlog/state raw and canonical hashes, the ACTIVE HOLD-W1-GRR-0002 identity within the hash-bound backlog, and the exact trigger witness. The new transaction and recover authority is limited to GCR-0002.B00 adoption recovery and grants no S02 installation, B02 implementation, historical-candidate exception, W1.A04 append, task action, T03 recovery, hold release, W1 resume, G1 approval, main integration, or remote action.

A focused synthesized transaction passes both the standalone transaction schema and runtime-v2 schema; wrong transaction identity, disabled write-through, wrong canonical paths in the top-level paths object, and an authority-bearing trigger are rejected. The incremental adversarial probe then demonstrates the remaining content-binding substitution: swapped nested CAS paths are accepted with zero transaction-schema errors.

Current backlog, approved GRR-0002, approved GRR-0002.S01, and adopted GCR-0001 validation all pass. All 22 affected taskctl schema tests pass in 45.232 seconds; governed Python quality passes over 121 files; and the exact six-path remediation diff passes Git whitespace hygiene.

The stopped boundary remains revision/minimum 8 with one ACTIVE HOLD-W1-GRR-0002, W1 PAUSED at wave scope, W1.A04 absent, CAP-02.S04.T03 BLOCKED, G1 PENDING, and the exact unstaged/untracked/non-authoritative witness as the sole untracked path. No canonical mutation or execution action was performed during this review.

GCR-0002-R01-F01 is not closed because its exact path-bound CAS requirement remains incomplete, and GCR-0002-R02-F01 records the reproducible residual schema gap. Human approval remains unavailable until a strict-descendant packet receives a fresh independent review that explicitly closes both findings.
